title: MS Dhoni Backs Solar Startup SolarSquare as It Raises $53 Million to Power Indian Homes
excerpt: Former India cricket captain MS Dhoni has invested in SolarSquare and joined as brand ambassador, as the rooftop solar startup's Series C round brings total funding past $100 million.
body:
• SolarSquare has raised $53 million in a Series C round led by B Capital, with participation from Lightspeed, Elevation Capital, Lowercarbon Capital, and Rainmatter.
  • Former India cricket captain MS Dhoni has invested through his family office Midas Deals and will serve as brand ambassador.
  • The Mumbai-based startup has powered approximately 50,000 homes across 29 cities and is running at an annual revenue rate of ₹1,000 crore ($114 million).
  • SolarSquare plans to expand into 30-40 new cities and move into battery storage, financing, and home energy management.

Dhoni Joins as Investor and Brand Ambassador

Former India cricket captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni has invested in rooftop solar startup SolarSquare through his family office, Midas Deals. As part of the deal, Dhoni will serve as the company's brand ambassador, lending his profile to a sector that has largely grown through word-of-mouth and government subsidies.

The investment is part of SolarSquare's $53 million Series C funding round, which was led by B Capital with participation from existing investors Lightspeed Venture Partners, Elevation Capital, Lowercarbon Capital, Rainmatter by Zerodha, and Good Capital, according to Inc42 and Mercom India. The round brings SolarSquare's total funding past $100 million.

"Five years ago, we made a conviction-led bet that every Indian home will be powered by rooftop solar. At the time, residential solar was still very nascent, with barely 1 lakh homes going solar per year. Today, the category has inflected, with 1 lakh homes adopting solar every 10 days in India."

— Shreya Mishra, Co-founder and CEO, SolarSquare

From Industrial to Residential Solar

Founded in 2015 by Shreya Mishra, Neeraj Jain, and Nikhil Nahar, SolarSquare initially served commercial and industrial customers before pivoting to residential rooftop solar in 2021. The shift proved prescient. The company now operates as a full-stack residential solar brand, handling everything from consultation and system design to installation, financing, monitoring, and maintenance.

SolarSquare has installed rooftop solar systems across approximately 50,000 homes and 400 housing societies in 29 cities, including Bengaluru, Delhi, and Hyderabad, as well as states like Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra. Its enterprise clients include Swiggy, Zepto, and iD Fresh Food, though residential customers and housing societies now account for a majority of the business, according to TechCrunch.

The company claims an annual revenue run rate of over ₹1,000 crore (approximately $114 million), and it aims to reach 200 megawatts in its residential solar portfolio this year.

Expansion Plans

SolarSquare will use the fresh capital to expand into 30 to 40 new cities, strengthen its technology platform, broaden financing options, enhance after-sales support, and ramp up hiring. The company also plans to move beyond rooftop solar installations into battery storage and home energy management solutions, positioning itself as a comprehensive home energy platform rather than a pure-play installer.

B Capital's Karan Mohla described SolarSquare's model as combining "category leadership, best-in-class unit economics, and a proprietary technology and asset-management layer that compounds with every install," according to a report by Entrepreneur.

India's Solar Market in Context

India's cumulative installed solar capacity has surged from about 3 GW in 2014 to more than 150 GW in 2026, making it the world's third-largest solar power producer behind China and the United States. The government's PM Surya Ghar subsidy scheme has accelerated residential adoption, while the country targets 500 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030.

However, the growth has not been without challenges. India's solar module manufacturing capacity has ballooned to over 200 GW, far outpacing domestic demand and creating what analysts call a structural glut. Cell manufacturing capacity remains a fraction of module capacity, with effective operating cell production at just 16-18 GW, according to EUPD Research. The resulting dependence on Chinese cell imports has left Indian manufacturers vulnerable to supply chain disruptions.

On the residential side, the opportunity remains vast. India has nearly 70 million rooftops suitable for solar installations, but penetration remains below 5%, according to SolarSquare. The company's Series B round in December 2024, a $40 million raise led by Lightspeed at around $200 million valuation, was then the largest solar venture investment in India.

What's Next

SolarSquare's latest round values the company between $450 million and $500 million, representing more than a doubling in roughly 18 months, TechCrunch reported. The Dhoni partnership adds consumer visibility to a category that is still early in its mainstream adoption curve. With Lowercarbon Capital — climate investor Chris Sacca's fund — among its backers since its early days, SolarSquare is positioning itself as the platform play in a market that remains dominated by small local installers and dealer networks.
nri_angle: SolarSquare's expansion across major Indian cities and its backing by global investors reflects the growing convergence of India's domestic clean energy push and international climate capital.
author: Diaspora Desk
